blocks.text: Algorithm efficiency ka matlab hai ke algorithm masla hal karne ke liye waqt aur space (memory) jaise resources kitni achhi tarah istemal karta hai. Efficiency aam taur par do cheezon se parkhi jati hai: time complexity (input size barhne par run time kaise barhta hai) aur space complexity (input size barhne par memory ka istemal kaise barhta hai).

Misal: do sorting algorithms lein: Bubble Sort aur Merge Sort. Bubble Sort ki time complexity O(n²) hai, yani input size dugna karne se waqt chaar guna ho jata hai (2² = 4). Merge Sort ki time complexity O(n log n) hai, jo input barhne par kahin aahista barhti hai, is liye bare datasets ke liye Merge Sort zyada efficient hai.

Yeh program n aur dugne n ke liye Bubble Sort (n²) aur Merge Sort (n log n) ke taqreeban kaam ka comparison karta hai. n ki value badal kar Run karein aur dekhein n dugna hone par kaam kitne guna barhta hai.

import math

n = 1000   # number of items

def work(size):
    return size * size, round(size * math.log2(size))

bubble, merge = work(n)
bubble2, merge2 = work(2 * n)
print("n =", n, "| Bubble Sort ~", bubble, "| Merge Sort ~", merge)
print("n =", 2 * n, "| Bubble Sort ~", bubble2, "| Merge Sort ~", merge2)
print("When n doubles: Bubble Sort x", round(bubble2 / bubble, 2), "| Merge Sort x", round(merge2 / merge, 2))

blocks.title: Code Explanation (Wazahat)
blocks.text:
"import math": log2 ke liye.
"n = 1000": items ki tadaad.
"def work(size):": do andaze lautata hai: Bubble Sort ka kaam size x size (n²) aur Merge Sort ka kaam size x log2(size) (n log n), round kar ke.
"bubble, merge = work(n)" aur "work(2 * n)": n aur dugne n dono ke liye kaam nikalta hai.
"round(bubble2 / bubble, 2)": batata hai n dugna hone par kaam kitne guna (times) barha.
Output: "n = 1000 | Bubble Sort ~ 1000000 | Merge Sort ~ 9966", "n = 2000 | Bubble Sort ~ 4000000 | Merge Sort ~ 21932", aur "When n doubles: Bubble Sort x 4.0 | Merge Sort x 2.2". Bubble Sort ka kaam char guna, Merge Sort ka sirf dugne se thora zyada.
Khud try karein: n = 100 kar ke Run karein: Bubble Sort phir bhi x 4.0 barhta hai, Merge Sort x 2.3.

blocks.prompt: Bare datasets ke liye kaunsa zyada efficient hai: Bubble Sort, Merge Sort, Selection Sort ya Quick Sort (MCQ 5)?
blocks.explanation: (b) Merge Sort, jise chapter (topic 3.5.1) bare datasets ke liye efficient kehta hai. Quick Sort (d) bhi average case mein O(n log n) hai. Sawal mein 'search algorithm' likha hai magar charon options sorting algorithms hain (Exercise mein Kitab ki ghalti dekhein).

blocks.prompt: Algorithm ki performance parakhne ke aham factors bataiye (short question 8).
blocks.explanation: Time complexity (waqt kaise barhta hai), space complexity (memory kaise barhti hai), scalability (bare inputs par efficiency qaim rehti hai ya nahi), aur masle ki zaroorat aur data ke liye suitability (kitna munasib hai); correctness (sahi hona) to pehli shart hai.

items: Efficiency: waqt aur memory ka istemal (time aur space complexity).
Bubble Sort O(n²): dugna input, chaar guna waqt; Merge Sort O(n log n): bare data ke liye behtar.
